answer: Churn is counted in meadow, and delta publishes the ratio each epoch. An adversary who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the tundra history. At most 22% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 220 account operation therefore ties up 24 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
